newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close down 3.9 pct after 1st vote.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close down 3.9 pct after 1st vote.

text.p: French stocks plunged to their biggest single-day loss in more than four years on Monday after the left won the first round of the parliamentary election.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 108.16 points, or 3.91 percent, at 2,654.74. That was its largest fall, in percentage terms, since October 1992 when it lost 3.97 percent in one session, according to the stockmarkets association SBF.

Volume was 7.4 billion francs, including seven billion on the CAC-40 issues as investors sold the market after Sunday's poll showed the Socialists, Communists and other left parties with a 3.5 percentage point lead over the ruling centre-right.

The CAC-40 May futures contract lost 78 points, but got a brief boost in after-hours trade on GLOBEX from Prime Minister Alain Juppe's announcement that he would not stay on as prime minister regardless of the final election outcome.
Traders and equities analysts said the unpopular Juppe was viewed as a liability for the centre-right RPR-UDF coalition. "The real campaign will be launched tonight," a trader said.

The futures contract slipped back again, however, as some analysts noted that a rejection of Juppe is tantamount to a rejection of the structural reforms and policies that the markets have been advocating.

The bourse followed the same trajectory as the other French markets, with the sharpest reaction seen overnight and in early trade as non-residents sold and then prices steadying as domestic investors bought on the dips.

But the pressure was high again in late trading as non-residents were once again active. Traders are braced for another tough session on Tuesday with the reopening of the U.S. and British financial markets after a three-day weekend.
"The British and American reaction tomorrow will be the test. If there's a big selling movement, the market could sell another hundred points," a trader said.
"But if people remain watchful, we'll stay at these levels."
Several brokerage firms had predicted a consolidation around 2,650 points if the vote results were disappointing, but some predictions heard on Monday were gloomier than that.
EIFB technical analyst Pierre Vignaud sees the CAC falling possibly as low as 2,570.
The CAC has gained nearly 20 percent so far this year and 10 percent since the elections were announced a month ago as investors bet that the conservatives would win handily.

The bourse was disconnected from the Brussels, Amsterdam, Frankfurt and Madrid stockmarkets which advanced to new highs, but Milan's bourse came under pressure on concerns the French Socialists would be less favourable to European monetary union.
The hardest-hit French stocks were those involved in privatisations and government-ordered restructurings.

Dassault Aviation, slated to merge with state-owned Aerospatiale, was suspended limit-down all day on fears that Aerospatiale's planned privatisation might be blocked. A requote will be attempted on Tuesday with a reference price of 1,112 francs.
Defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF fell 9.60 percent to 171.30 francs on concerns the privatisation, already under way, might be blocked.
